recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add duplicate transaction-order text or new operation-order rules without a new work-group decision, because the discovered evidence identifies operations as hard to classify but does not show a final decision requiring a current source change.
issue_request: FHIR-34060 asked for the HTTP transaction processing rules to use FHIR interactions instead of raw HTTP verbs because method-only ordering made POST search, PUT create/update, and GET operation cases ambiguous. The final Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution said to use FHIR interactions while still retaining HTTP verb descriptions where helpful.
initial_application: Commit faaaefb02fd5801ae42a282443d030a423b04cee explicitly applied FHIR-34060 by changing source/http.html from DELETE/POST/PUT/PATCH/GET method-only ordering to linked FHIR interaction names: delete, create, update, patch, read, vread, search, and history, with parenthetical HTTP verbs. The current source retains that wording.
additional_context: The 2021 Zulip discussion and FHIR-I minutes show the work group recognized that transaction order affects interoperability and that POST-based search and operations were edge cases. Later FHIR-36095 specifically clarified POST-based search in batch/transaction Bundles by saying searches should be accepted via GET and that POST-based searches have no standard Bundle representation; that related issue is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/http.html already uses FHIR interaction names in the transaction order and preserves HTTP verb annotations allowed by the resolution. source/search.html separately resolves the POST-search-in-Bundle ambiguity that motivated part of FHIR-34060.

related_jiras.note: Clarified the POST-based search in batch/transaction Bundle ambiguity by requiring GET acceptance and noting there is no standard POST-search Bundle representation; already audited on the combined branch.
Defined POST-based search variants for ordinary REST search endpoints, explaining the POST-search concern but not changing the Bundle-specific transaction conclusion.
